articles.title: Thanksgiving in a Cost of Living Crisis
articles.summary: This Thanksgiving, Marni Charnow, a 32-year-old tech consultant, drove 21 hours to her family’s home in Southern Florida to celebrate Thanksgiving. She started from her house in Birmingham, Michigan, with her cats in the back seat, all to save on the now-astronomical cost of airfare for herself and her pets. She’d budgeted for the hotel and gas costs for her travel, yet she still has to work all of next week and the weekends to be able to pay for the voyage back and other expenses. articles.title: I’m a Doctor With Stage 4 Cancer. Even I Struggled to Get My Insurance to Pay
articles.summary: Without insurance, emergency department or urgent care visits are completely unaffordable for the average person. In 2021, the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) estimated the average cost in the United States for a “treat and release” Emergency Department visit is $750. The bill could be much, much higher, even thousands of dollars, depending on tests performed and treatment administered. articles.title: How to Have a More Sustainable Black Friday, According to Experts
articles.summary: Black Friday is here—holding the promise of good deals and the unofficial start of the holiday shopping season. But if you plan to shop the sales, take the time to think about what you really need —and what you plan to give. Americans spent $10 billion dollars on unwanted gifts in 2024. And last year, 65% of consumers reported returning a holiday gift, while 54% admitted to regifting an unwanted item.
